shared_head:
You are one lane of a 20-wide wave in the local_sovereign_agent fleet ("the mesh") — a file-first AI operation: signed chain of record, tri-state claims (Supported/Disputed/Unproven, evidence attached), one-builds-one-verifies, no seat is load-bearing. Operator runs a laptop + Docker cage; a 4x Mac Studio M5 Ultra ("Rocinante") lands ~Oct 27. Standing organs: hermes CLI (cron/approvals/checkpoints), verkle chain, watch/ cards, topic_index (1,040 cards), organ table, Build 3.5 (vault/ack-reaper/steer-signing/lesson gate), wave drivers, the NEW fanout organ (mag/fanout.py: packs are JSON data, stdin/stdout, zero file I/O in cage).

TODAY'S MISSION: hunt MISSING ORGANS. The architecture just revealed two of its own gaps by HOW IT FAILED: (1) three N-wide firings each wrote a throwaway runner that evaporated — there was no standing fan-out organ until today; (2) at 944K-token context the boot law is ~0.05% of input and the reply register flooded with drift — behavior salience decays and nothing scans for it. Your lane hunts ONE more gap of this species: a missing organ the architecture implies, PROVEN by a repeating pattern, spec'd as v0.

HOUSE LAWS: plain English, no moon-speak. Tri-state every borrowed claim. Mark UNPROVEN where you extrapolate. Be concrete: name files, steps, and costs.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: markdown, 500-900 words, exactly these sections:
## Verdict
(one line: the missing organ and whether it's real)
## Pattern
(what repeats, with the specific evidence from CONTEXT — duplication is emphasis)
## Invariant
(the compiled law this organ enforces, one sentence)
## Organ v0
(spec: inputs, outputs, where it lives, who runs it, the one acceptance test)
## Falsifier
(how we'd know the organ is wrong or unnecessary)
## File to
(one repo path)

lanes.context: The boot file (AGENTS.md) is 500+ lines with the operator's laws buried mid-file; the live arc section froze 09-11. At 944K-token context the law is ~0.05% of input and drift happens anyway. This morning's operator corrections were ALL re-derivations of laws that already existed (file every paste; English-only; self-steal before rebuilding). A drift canary (scanning surfaces for CJK + unfilinged pastes) is being armed separately — but catching drift is only half; the law that was drifted past must get LOUDER next boot.
lanes.task: Spec the SALIENCE-CARD organ: a one-screen generated 'morning laws' card, machine-ranked by drift frequency (which laws the canary actually caught being violated, most-caught on top), regenerated at each wave fold from canary catches, pointed to by one stable line in the boot file so the boot file itself never needs re-editing. How does a catch increment a law's rank? What keeps it data not instruction? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The seat fired a 20-lane wave from a memory 'recipe' note instead of reading the actual runner — the note said 'verified 09-12' but referenced script shapes that had already evaporated. Separately, 2 of 7 'free' rows in the model zoo were dead as listed: catalog listing is not servable. Memory notes that describe PROCEDURES decay silently while still sounding authoritative.
lanes.task: Spec the RECIPE_VERIFIER organ: every memory/card that encodes a procedure carries a verify-command (one command that proves the procedure still works) and a verified-date; the librarian's audit sweeps for stale recipes (verified >N days) and flags them DISPUTED-stale in place (append, never delete). What's the verify-command for a recipe about a script that no longer exists? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: Today's p20 wave persisted its outputs to memory/runs/p20_pending_wave_20260912/ — but yesterday's dozen-wide wave left NO outputs and NO runner anywhere (mag/, scripts/, container /tmp all empty). Folds cannot find prior waves; the only pointer to yesterday's run was one line in a memory index. Each wave is a major spend event with no register row.
lanes.task: Spec the WAVE_LEDGER organ: one append-only register every fanout run must produce a row in (run id, date, pack path, model, width, completion tokens, outputs path, fold card path). The fanout organ is stdin/stdout only and writes no files — so decide honestly WHO appends the row (the host redirect step? a hermes cron sweep? the fold?). Reconcile with the librarian's unregistered-dust audit. Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: fanout.py marks a lane OK if text is non-empty — green means 'returned something', not 'returned the deliverable'. The dozen-wide wave found 5 of 12 lanes passing a night test FALSLEY (vacuous green: idle box reports success). Lane outputs are contracted to carry 5 house sections (Verdict/Body/Next steps/Tri-state/File to). Today's fold claimed 20/20 clean based on spot-checking 2 of 20 files by hand.
lanes.task: Spec the LANE_VERIFIER organ: a deterministic (no-LLM) checker run host-side after each fanout split — section presence, tri-state section present, length bounds, CJK-character scan for register drift, invented-fact heuristics if cheap. Fold cards then cite verified counts (17/20 verified) instead of green counts (20/20). Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: fanout.py reads exactly ONE key env var (ZAI_API_KEY_Lite). The cage holds ZAI_API_KEY_Lite, ZAI_API_KEY_Pro (parked), DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (clean, pennies); groq is CF-blocked from the cage, gemini key 403s. Yesterday's session hit 1302 rate-limit errors at width 20 on coding-plan lanes. One key at width 4 works but a bigger wave or a congested day has no fallback path.
lanes.task: Spec KEY-POOL rotation for the fanout pack format: a keys[] field (env var names, never values), round-robin assignment across lanes, 1302/429 backoff that retries on a different key, per-key pace caps from configs/providers.yaml notes, and spend attribution per key in the summary JSON. What stays true if ALL keys are congested (queue vs fail-honest)? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The default-actuation law says a recommendation executes in 48h unless vetoed; only 4 gates stay with the operator (spend GOs, KEYS, ONE STOP, publish GO). Today's sign-sheet adjudication said: 'post the per-item assent/veto words to hermes approvals so the clocks run on record rather than on ambient silence.' Right now the 48h windows exist in prose — sign sheet (7 items), mint consents (3 drafts), opik install (recommended) — with NO tracked deadline anywhere.
lanes.task: Spec the VETO_CLOCK organ: every default-actuation recommendation opens a hermes approvals row carrying {item, recommendation, deadline, veto word, assent word}; expiry produces a signed record row and THEN execution (record-before-act); the operator sees all open clocks in one surface. What happens if hermes is down at expiry? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: Wave lanes constantly emit 'next step: run X' items that evaporate — today's sign-sheet adjudication said 'one grep resolves 4 of 7 states' and nobody has run it. UNFETCHED markers sit scattered across watch/inbox cards from different days. The architecture generates cheap pending probes faster than any seat remembers them.
lanes.task: Spec the PENDING_PROBES register: every fold extracts its lanes' cheap local next-steps into one register (id, probe, source card, cost estimate, status); a cron or pulse cycle drains it oldest-first; done rows cite their receipt. How does it dedupe against topic_index and avoid becoming a junk drawer? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The fleet's own memory index (MEMORY.md) hit 256 lines / 56KB and the loader now TRUNCATES it — 'only part of it was loaded.' The index that exists to prevent amnesia has itself become partially amnesiac. House rule already says one line per memory under ~200 chars with detail in topic files, but nothing enforces it.
lanes.task: Spec the MEMORY_GARDENER organ: compaction cadence, the move-detail-to-topic-file rule as a mechanical check (line length, file size), prune rules (what earns deletion vs archival), who runs it (cron? seat at fold?), and how it stays reversible (archived lines recoverable). Acceptance test: a fact lost to truncation gets caught by the gardener BEFORE a seat needs it. Falsifier.

lanes.context: The boot file's 'Current arc' section froze at the 09-11 wave; state/CURRENT.md froze 09-08; live status actually lives in watch/ fold cards. The operator re-reads a stale arc every boot, and new seats get a stale picture on day one. The architecture has no single live-status surface that is itself regenerated.
lanes.task: Spec the ARC_POINTER organ: ONE generated card (chain tip, open falsifiers, armed crons + their last fire, pending operator decisions, current wave) regenerated at every fold, with the boot file pointing to its PATH once and never being edited again. What does it do when a fold doesn't happen for 48h (staleness marker)? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: Model quirks live in prose memory: glm-5.3-flash needs >=8192 max_tokens (thinking eats the budget, 2048 returns EMPTY), creative-register prompts cook it even at 24K; deepseek-chat is clean; gemini key 403s on 3.6; groq is CF-blocked from the cage; Nous :free rows died as listed. fanout.py hardcodes ONE model's defaults; every new lane author must re-learn the quirks from prose.
lanes.task: Spec the MODEL_SPECS register: machine-readable rows {model, key_env, base, max_tokens_floor, thinking_behavior, register_hazards, verified_date} that packs reference by name; probes (not catalog listings) are the only way a row becomes Supported; how fanout consumes it without file I/O (pack generator inlines the row). Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: Today's p20 wave spent 107,483 completion tokens and the fold card says 'pennies' — with no dollar figure anywhere. kpi.jsonl (457MB, continuous since Jul-21) holds raw call history. The operator budgets time and money like quota but no wave has ever reported an actual measured cost line.
lanes.task: Spec the SPEND_ROLLUP organ: per-wave $ (completion tokens x model price from a price table, cached-token discount noted), per-day and per-key rollups, computed host-side after each fanout split (the summary JSON already carries token counts). Where does the price table live and how does it stay honest (prices change)? Fold cards gain one '$ line'. Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The intake-wave cron was armed today with the falsifier 'first autonomous receipt in CONVO by ~2h' — no organ checks whether an armed falsifier actually fired. The proposed day-0 watch (L19) adds a 30-min cron with an SLO ('alert within one tick; delta >60m = a miss'). Pulse (the C1 heart candidate) needs exactly this feed: gates can only be judged if armed promises are tracked.
lanes.task: Spec the FALSIFIER_TRACKER organ: armed crons/promises register {promise, deadline, receipt-where, status}; a pulse-cycle or cron sweep flips status fired/missed; a missed falsifier becomes a Disputed chain row (loud death). How does the tracker itself stay honest (who watches the watcher)? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The operator's Desktop 'New folder' holds 248 hand-saved files (245MB) — walked once in the 09-11 record-pool census. TODAY a hand-exported trajectory file saved there became the primary evidence for diagnosing the drift/amnesia mechanism. The operator's hand layer is a primary source that the architecture only sees when someone remembers to walk it.
lanes.task: Spec the DESKTOP_INTAKE organ: how hand-saves get hashed + indexed into topic_index WITHOUT moving the original (the hand layer is sacred — desk edits never re-voice), what cadence, what stays private (never echo contents to external lanes), and how a new file in that folder becomes visible to the next fold. Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The operator had to MANUALLY export a session trajectory file to his desktop to debug the Chinese-drift mechanism. Session artifacts live in zcode CLI directories; the orphan-grounding wave hashed 16,500 of them once (memory/ = 96.6% of workload) but there is no standing tailer — drift evidence exists only if someone hand-copies it in time.
lanes.task: Spec the SESSION_VAULT_TAILER organ: a cron that hashes NEW session artifacts into the existing vault so any drift conversation is retrievable without hand-export; bounds (never echo secrets or credentials into cards; hashes + paths only until a lane is explicitly asked); retention. Acceptance test: tomorrow's drift file is findable by the canary without the operator lifting a finger. Falsifier.

lanes.context: This week's waves (p20 pending, dozen-wide, mint 9-wide, W-wave 9-wide) each wrote fresh lens text for overlapping subjects — the organ table, Rocinante day-0, day-0 watch, Obsidian surfaces were lensed at least twice each. Packs are now data (fanout.json) but lens FRAGMENTS are not reused, and cross-lane cache hits only work within one run's shared head.
lanes.task: Spec the LENS_INDEX organ: reusable lens fragments registered {id, text, topic, last_used, times_used}; a pack builder composes shared heads + lane lenses FROM the index (maximizing the cached prefix across runs); staleness rule. Note the cache economics honestly (shared-prefix hits measured at 320 tokens today — small; is reuse worth it beyond cache?). Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: Today's Opik-reconciliation (L20) makes the trajectory-envelope change safe ONLY if a null span field keeps serialization byte-identical — 'every existing chain entry still verifies' is the acceptance test. Chain v1 is FROZEN as the advisor's source of record; GROUNDING_WAVE rows are a v3 format verified across foreign seats. Hash-chained formats have NO standing compatibility tests — every schema change is a silent-corruption risk taken on prose alone.
lanes.task: Spec the SCHEMA_COMPAT_TESTER organ: golden-file tests for every hash-chained format (trajectory envelope, GROUND rows, chain knots, lesson-gate registry, canary commits); old records must verify under the NEW code, every time, run at pulse-cycle or pre-merge. What is the golden corpus and who freezes it? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The operator reads on his phone and the state he needs is scattered: CONVO rows, fold cards, sign sheet, approvals queue, armed crons, spend. The tide protocol defined a 'day fact sheet' for salon chairs; overseer.json already feeds a dashboard strip; but there is no single operator-facing surface answering: what fired overnight, what needs my hand, what's broken, what did it cost.
lanes.task: Spec the DAY_SHEET organ: one generated page regenerated at every fold — who's guarding what, decisions awaiting, falsifiers fired/missed, spend line, drift-canary catches — phone-first formatting, rendered to dashboard/static like overseer.json. What does it show when nothing happened (the vacuous-green trap)? Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The open-journal protocol: operator hand-writes one decision/day, photographs it, the seat transcribes verbatim same-turn (Day 1 and Day 2 landed this way); drift copies preserved; desk edits never re-voice. But intake depends on the operator AND a seat being in the same conversation — photos left on the desktop or in screenshots sit untranscribed when he's away.
lanes.task: Spec the JOURNAL_INTAKE organ: how a new hand-page photo gets noticed (via the desktop intake pattern), staged safely (marked AWAITING-TRANSCRIPTION, never auto-voiced by a lane — transcription is a judgment seat's act), and reconciled with the 'silence is valid' law. Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: This week two lanes (R18 and C1-8) independently polished the SAME noth-ethrium annex — duplicate work discovered only at fold. Agent spawn warnings say 'do not duplicate this agent's work' but nothing enforces it across waves. At doctrine level duplication is emphasis (pheromones); at execution level it is waste — the architecture never distinguishes the two.
lanes.task: Spec the COLLISION_GUARD organ: claim-before-work rows {lane, target file, intent, ttl} in a register that spawners consult before dispatch; an expired claim releases; a duplicate claim becomes ALLOWED emphasis only when explicitly flagged as verification/redundancy (the mesh WANTS redundant verification — one-builds-one-verifies). Reconcile with stigmergy doctrine. Acceptance test + falsifier.

lanes.context: The sacred-cow audit found the recurring weakness: 'the record is append-only but nothing declares its own death' — GROUNDING_WAVE went dark silently for days; the chain froze Sep-6 for days before anyone noticed; the ollama eye does not auto-start and sat dark 12h at boot. Files do not scream when they stop. The wave driver spec names a 'loud-death klaxon' as v1 work not yet built.
lanes.task: Spec the LOUD_DEATH organ: TTL witnesses on every append surface (GROUNDING_WAVE, chain knots, cron receipts, CONVO rows, the eye at 127.0.0.1:11434) — a surface with no heartbeat inside its TTL is DISPUTED-dead, loudly, at the next pulse cycle or fold; recovery flips it back with a receipt. This is the organ pulse (the C1 heart) reads first. Acceptance test + falsifier.
